data.narrative:
Senra Systems is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $112M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of three same-stage, same-sector comparables—Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B)—supplemented by a broader set of nine private robotics firms and one public comparable.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy for post-money valuation, applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, implying $213M. Peer-median valuation across the three same-stage comparables yields $1.8B, with the range spanning $1.6B to $2.0B. The stark divergence between these methods reflects the thinness of the early-stage robotics comp set and uncertainty around whether Senra's technology positioning and traction align with the higher-valued peers in the sample.

The triangulated analysis supports a broad range from $181M (floor) to $2.0B (ceiling), with a median of $981M. The stage-progression method anchors the lower bound; peer-median dominates the upper end. Key uncertainties include the degree to which Senra's commercial traction and proprietary capabilities merit valuation at the peer median versus a significant discount, and whether the public comparable and broader private set would narrow this range materially with deeper operational diligence.
